to teach / to instruct / to show / to point out; Verb meaning to give lessons in a school or a university, or to show someone how a specific task or machine works.
to instruct / to inform / to educate / to investigate (a case); Verb meaning to give specific knowledge or orders to someone, or for a judge to prepare a legal case by gathering evidence.

to initiate / to introduce / to start / to admit to a secret; Verb meaning to show someone the basic steps of a new activity for the first time, or to allow someone to join a secret group or knowledge.

to assimilate / to digest (knowledge) / to equate / to integrate; Verb meaning to fully understand and remember new information, or for a minority group to become like the majority culture, or to compare two different things as being the same.
to memorize / to commit to memory / to store (data); Verb meaning to learn something so well that you can remember it perfectly later, or for a computer to save data.
to revise / to review / to overhaul / to check; Verb meaning to study again what you have already learned for an exam, to change an opinion or a law, or to repair a machine thoroughly.
to scrutinize / to peer at / to scan / to examine closely; Verb meaning to look at something very carefully and for a long time to find out a secret or to see every small detail.
to analyze / to examine / to break down / to parse; Verb meaning to study a complex thing by looking at each of its small parts to understand how it works or what it means.

to interpret / to play (a role/music) / to translate (orally); Verb meaning to explain the meaning of a dream or a text, to perform a song or a role in a specific style, or to translate spoken words from one language to another.
to translate / to express / to manifest / to bring to court; Verb meaning to change a text or speech from one language to another, or for an action to be a clear sign of a feeling.

to transcribe / to copy out / to record / to adapt (music); Verb meaning to write down exactly what someone is saying, to copy a text into another book, or to change a piece of music for a different instrument.
to copy / to imitate / to cheat / to burn (a CD); Verb meaning to make an exact double of a document or a drawing, to behave exactly like someone else, or to look at someone's exam paper illegally.

to imitate / to mimic / to counterfeit / to follow the example of; Verb meaning to copy the voice or movements of a person to be funny, or to use someone as a model for how to live, or to make a fake product look real.
to reproduce / to replicate / to breed / to happen again; Verb meaning to make a copy of a picture, for animals/plants to have babies, or for an event to happen for a second time exactly like before.
to engender / to beget / to generate / to cause; Verb meaning for a biological father to beget a child, or figuratively for a situation or an action to cause a specific result or a new feeling.
to generate / to produce / to create / to spawn; Modern verb meaning to produce something using a system or a machine (like electricity, profits, or a computer report).
to manufacture / to make / to fabricate / to invent (a lie); Verb meaning to make products in a factory using machines, or figuratively to invent a story or a lie that is not true.
to make / to prepare / to put together / to fashion; Verb meaning to prepare a meal with care or to make clothes (often used for high-quality manual work).
to elaborate / to work out / to devise / to develop; Verb meaning to work hard and carefully to create a complex plan, a theory, or a strategy.
to cogitate / to ponder / to think hard / to rack one's brains; Informal or slightly ironic verb meaning to think very deeply about a problem for a long time, often looking for a clever solution.
to meditate / to ponder / to contemplate / to plan (in secret); Verb meaning to think deeply in silence (often for religious reasons), or to think very carefully about a future action or a revenge.

to speculate / to theorize / to gamble (on the market); Verb meaning to guess about the future without having all the facts, or to buy things (like stocks) hoping their price will go up so you can make a profit.
to reason / to argue / to talk sense into / to think logically; Verb meaning to use logic to reach a conclusion, or to try to convince someone to be calm and sensible by explaining the facts.
to argue / to plead / to state one's case / to give reasons; Verb meaning to give a set of reasons to prove that something is true or to convince someone to do something.
to debate / to discuss / to argue / to struggle; Verb meaning to discuss a topic formally in a group where different people have different opinions, or to struggle with a problem.
to palaver / to talk at length / to waffle / to discuss endlessly; Pejorative verb meaning to talk for a very long time without reaching a decision, often about small or useless details.
to converse / to chat / to talk with someone; Formal verb meaning to have a conversation with another person in a polite and friendly way.
to dialogue / to talk / to have a discussion; Verb meaning for two people or two groups (like governments) to talk to each other to understand their different views and find a solution.
to communicate / to convey / to pass on / to be in touch; Verb meaning to share information or feelings with someone through speaking, writing, or body language, or for two rooms to be connected.
to broadcast / to diffuse / to spread / to release; Verb meaning to send out a program or news by radio/TV, to let a smell or light move through a room, or to make an idea known to many people.
to propagate / to spread / to transmit / to multiply; Verb meaning to make a sound, a feeling, or a disease move from one place to another, or to spread a specific belief among the public.
to spread / to scatter / to spill / to shed (tears); Verb meaning to accidentally let a liquid fall out of its container, or to intentionally make a smell or a news reach everywhere.

to scatter / to strew / to spread out / to waste (energy); Verb meaning to throw things in many different directions so they are not in one pile, or figuratively to use your time/energy on too many small things at once.

to disperse / to scatter / to break up (a crowd) / to dissipate; Verb meaning for a group of people or objects to move away from each other in different directions, often because the police or the wind forced them.
to dissipate / to clear up / to waste / to dispel; Verb meaning to make a feeling (like fear or doubt) or a cloud vanish, or to spend your money or your life in a very foolish and wasteful way.
to waste / to squander / to throw away / to lose (an opportunity); Verb meaning to use money, time, or an advantage in a very bad way so that you get no benefit from it and it is gone forever.
to save / to spare / to economize / to exempt; Verb meaning to keep money for the future instead of spending it, or to choose not to hurt or kill someone who is in your power.
to save / to economize / to cut down on / to reduce usage; Verb meaning to use less of something (like water, electricity, or energy) so that you don't run out or so you spend less money.
to invest / to surround / to grant power / to inhabit; Verb meaning to put money into a business to get more back later, or for an army to surround a city, or to officially give someone a high rank.
to sponsor / to godparent / to endorse / to mentor; Verb meaning to give money to support a project or an athlete, or to act as a godparent for a child, or to help a new employee join a company.
to finance / to fund / to bankroll / to pay for; Verb meaning to provide the necessary money for a big project, a war, or a movie to be made.
to subsidize / to grant aid / to help financially; Verb meaning for the government or a large organization to give a grant of money to keep a service (like trains) cheap or to help an artist.
to stake / to bet / to count on / to rely on; Verb meaning to put a specific amount of money on a game, or figuratively to put all your hope and effort into one person or one idea.
to play the stock market / to dabble in stocks / to speculate; Slightly informal verb meaning to buy and sell small amounts of company shares (stocks) hoping to make a quick profit.
to bet / to wager / to guarantee / to pledge; Verb meaning to bet on a result, or to guarantee that something will happen (often used in fixed phrases like "je gage que..." - I bet that...).
to guarantee / to back / to support / to vouch for; Verb meaning to provide a financial guarantee for a debt, or figuratively to give your approval and support to a person or an idea.
to guarantee / to warrant / to protect / to ensure; Verb meaning to promise that a product will work for a long time or that a fact is 100% true, or to protect someone from a danger.
to certify / to attest / to vouch for / to confirm officially; Verb meaning to officially state that something is true or that a document is real, usually by signing a paper.
to corroborate / to confirm / to back up / to strengthen; Formal verb meaning to provide new evidence or facts that prove that someone else's story or theory is true.
to attest / to bear witness / to certify / to show; Verb meaning to show clearly that something exists or is true, or to serve as official proof of an event.
to testify / to deposit / to put down / to remove (a king); Verb meaning to state facts in a court of law, to put money in a bank, or to take off a crown or a president from power.
to affirm / to assert / to state / to maintain; Verb meaning to state something very strongly and clearly as being true, especially when other people might doubt it.

to declare / to state / to pronounce / to report (taxes); Verb meaning to make an official public statement, or to tell the government how much money you earned or what you are bringing into the country.
to proclaim / to announce / to herald / to shout out; Verb meaning to announce something very important and official in a loud or solemn way, often used for new laws, independence, or winners.
to divulge / to reveal / to leak / to make public; Verb meaning to make known something that was supposed to be secret, like a government document or a private conversation.
to unveil / to reveal / to uncover / to disclose; Verb meaning to remove a veil from a statue, or figuratively to reveal the truth about a mystery or a hidden plan for the first time.
to mask / to hide / to disguise / to cover up; Verb meaning to cover someone's face with a mask, or figuratively to hide a bad feeling or a physical defect so other people don't notice it.
to dissimulate / to conceal / to hide / to pretend not to notice; Verb meaning to hide your real feelings or a physical object on purpose, often to trick someone or to avoid a difficult situation.
to occult / to obscure / to hide / to eclipse; Formal verb meaning to intentionally hide information from the public, or for one planet to hide the light of another star.
to camouflage / to disguise / to hide / to cover up; Verb meaning to hide an object (like a tank or a building) by making it look like the things around it, or figuratively to hide a scandal.
to disguise / to dress up / to mask / to conceal; Verb meaning to change your appearance with clothes and a wig so no one knows who you are, or to change the truth to make it look better.

to travesty / to misrepresent / to distort / to parody; Verb meaning to describe a fact or a thought in a way that is totally wrong and unfair, or to dress up in the clothes of the opposite sex for a play.
to denature / to distort / to alter / to spoil; Verb meaning to change the natural quality of a substance, or figuratively to report words or facts in a way that changes their original meaning.
to falsify / to distort / to warp / to throw off; Verb meaning to bend a tool so it doesn't work, or to change numbers/data to tell a lie, or for a singer to sing out of tune.
to alter / to impair / to distort / to make thirsty; Verb meaning to change something in a way that makes it worse (like health or a document), or to make someone feel very thirsty.
to amend / to improve / to fertilize / to correct; Verb meaning to make small changes to a law or a text to improve it, or to add fertilizer to the soil to make it better for plants.
to rectify / to correct / to adjust / to distill; Verb meaning to put right a mistake or an unfair situation, or to adjust a mathematical line, or to purify a liquid through heat.
to correct / to mark / to edit / to punish; Verb meaning to find and fix mistakes in a student's paper, to make a machine work accurately, or to physically punish someone for their behavior.
to sanction / to punish / to approve / to confirm officially; Verb with two opposite meanings: to officially punish someone for a crime, or to officially approve a new law or a custom.
to chastise / to punish / to refine (style); Formal verb meaning to punish someone severely to correct them, or figuratively to make your writing style very pure and perfect.
to repress / to crack down on / to restrain (feelings); Verb meaning to use force to stop a revolt, or to prevent yourself from showing an emotion (like a laugh or a tear).
to oppress / to crush / to weigh down; Verb meaning to treat a group of people in an unfair and cruel way by taking away their freedom, or for a feeling of sadness to weigh heavily on your heart.
to enslave / to subjugate / to dominate / to make dependent; Verb meaning to turn a person into a slave, or for a passion (like gambling) to control someone so they are no longer free to choose.
to vassalize / to subordinate / to make a satellite (state); Formal verb meaning for one country to force another country to follow all its orders, effectively turning it into a servant-state.
to subject / to subdue / to fasten / to make dependent; Verb meaning to force a person or a group to follow your rules, or to mechanically fasten a piece of metal or wood so it cannot move.
to subordinate / to make secondary / to make dependent on; Verb meaning to put something in a lower rank of importance, or to make the success of a plan depend entirely on one specific condition.
to constrain / to force / to compel / to restrain; Verb meaning to force someone to do something against their will, often by using physical power, a law, or a strong moral feeling.
to enjoin / to charge / to order formally / to prescribe; Formal verb meaning to give a clear and strict order to someone to do something, usually as an authority figure or a judge.

to prescribe / to order / to direct / to become void (law); Verb meaning for a doctor to order a medicine, for a law to require a specific action, or for a legal right to expire because too much time has passed.
to decree / to order / to proclaim / to decide arbitrarily; Verb meaning to make an official decision that has the power of law, often done by a president or a king without asking others.
to promulgate / to enact / to publish (a law) / to spread; Formal verb meaning to officially sign a law that has been voted so it can finally be used and followed by everyone.
to legislate / to make laws / to enact rules; Verb meaning to create or discuss new laws in a parliament or a government body.
to establish / to set up / to initiate / to restore; Verb meaning to start a new system, a custom, or a regime that is intended to last for a long time.
to institute / to establish / to set up / to appoint; Verb meaning to create a formal organization, a law, or a ceremony, or to officially name someone as an heir.
to edify / to build / to construct / to enlighten; Verb meaning to build a large monument or a complex theory, or figuratively to improve someone's mind or character by giving them a good example.
to erect / to set up / to build / to raise to the rank of; Verb meaning to build a vertical monument like a statue, or to officially change the status of a village into a city.

to frame / to structure / to build the framework of / to skeletonize; Verb meaning to build the wooden frame of a house or a ship, or figuratively to give a strong and logical structure to a book or a speech.
to structure / to organize / to arrange / to format; Verb meaning to give a clear and organized shape to a collection of parts so they work together as a whole system.

to orchestrate / to arrange (music) / to coordinate / to stage; Verb meaning to arrange music for many instruments, or figuratively to plan and coordinate a complex event or a secret campaign so everything happens at the right time.
to coordinate / to align / to organize together; Verb meaning to make different parts of a complex plan or different people work together in an efficient and balanced way.
to arrange / to lay out / to fit / to fix up; Verb meaning to organize pieces of furniture or parts of a machine in a specific space to make it look good or work perfectly.
to dispose / to arrange / to set out / to have at one's disposal; Verb meaning to put things in a specific place, or to have something (like money or time) that you are free to use whenever you want.
to rule / to govern / to manage / to boss around; Slightly pejorative verb meaning to rule a country or a house in a very strict and bossy way, as if you are the only one with power.
to enact / to decree / to issue / to lay down; Formal verb meaning for an authority to officially create a new rule or a law that everyone must follow immediately.
to manage / to lead / to handle (a team) / to run; Modern verb (from English) meaning to lead a team of workers, to organize their tasks, and to make sure the business goals are reached.
to pilot / to fly / to steer / to lead a project; Verb meaning to operate an airplane or a ship, or figuratively to be the main person in charge of a complex project to make sure it succeeds.
to escort / to convoy / to accompany / to guard; Verb meaning to go with a person or a ship to protect them from danger or to show them honor.
to direct / to steer / to switch / to orient; Verb meaning to move a train to a different track, or figuratively to give advice to someone that puts them on a specific career or life path.
to orient / to direct / to position / to guide; Verb meaning to place an object in a specific direction (like towards the sun), or to help someone choose their future job or study.
to position / to place / to situate / to market (a product); Verb meaning to put an object in a very precise spot, or to market a product in a way that appeals to a specific group of people.
to install / to settle / to set up / to seat; Verb meaning to put a machine or software in place so it can be used, or to settle into a new house or a comfortable chair.
to lodge / to house / to put up / to be located; Verb meaning to provide a room for someone to stay in, or for an object (like a bullet) to be stuck inside something else.
to host / to house / to accommodate / to host (a website); Verb meaning to let someone stay in your house for a short time, or for a server to store and show a website on the internet.
to receive / to take delivery of / to catch (a ball) / to accept; Technical verb meaning to officially take a package or a building from a contractor after checking that it is correct.
to admit / to allow / to accept / to let in; Verb meaning to allow someone to enter a place like a school or a club, or to accept that a fact is true even if it is unpleasant.
to tolerate / to allow / to endure / to put up with; Verb meaning to allow something to happen or exist even if you don't like it or agree with it, without trying to stop it.
to empower / to authorize / to qualify / to entitle; Formal verb meaning to give someone the legal right or the necessary skills to perform a specific task or to sign a document.
to authorize / to allow / to permit / to sanction; Verb meaning to give official permission for an action to take place, often by a person in a high position or by a law.

to mandate / to commission / to authorize (to act for another) / to pay (official); Formal verb meaning to officially give someone the power to act or vote in your name, or to order a government payment to be made.
to delegate / to depute / to assign (authority) / to entrust; Verb meaning to give part of your work or your power to someone else (usually a subordinate) so they can do it for you.
to mission / to assign a mission / to send on a task; Verb meaning to give someone a very specific and important goal to reach, often involving a journey or a secret task.
to affect / to assign / to allocate / to pretend; Verb meaning to give a specific job or room to someone, or to have a physical effect on something, or to fake a feeling.
to attribute / to assign / to grant / to award; Verb meaning to officially give a prize, a task, or a property to someone, or to state that a work of art was made by a specific person.
to grant / to bestow / to vouchsafe / to give as a favor; Formal verb meaning for a high authority (like a king or a state) to give a right or a privilege to someone as a special favor.
to accord / to grant / to tune / to match / to reconcile; Verb meaning to give permission or a right, or to adjust a musical instrument so it sounds right, or for two ideas to match each other.
to concede / to grant / to give in / to admit (defeat); Verb meaning to let someone have something because they fought for it, or to admit that an opponent is right about a specific point.
to retrocede / to hand back / to cede back / to transfer back; Legal verb meaning to give back a territory or a right to its original owner after holding it for some time.
to restore / to return / to give back / to recreate; Verb meaning to give back an object to its owner, or to restore an image or a sound to its original clear quality using technology.
to pay back / to transfer (funds) / to pour back / to rebate; Verb meaning to pay back a sum of money to a specific person or to transfer funds from one budget to another.

to compensate / to offset / to make up for / to counterbalance; Verb meaning to give something good to someone who has suffered a loss or a pain, or to use one thing to balance the bad effect of another thing.
to indemnify / to compensate / to make amends / to pay damages; Verb meaning to pay money to someone because you broke their property or caused them a physical or emotional injury.
to indemnify / to compensate / to pay back for a loss; Formal verb used mainly by insurance companies or governments to pay money to people who lost their homes or jobs in a disaster.
to reimburse / to pay back / to refund / to repay (a debt); Verb meaning to give back money that you borrowed, or to return money to a customer who is unhappy with a product.
to remunerate / to pay / to reward / to recompense; Formal verb meaning to give money or a reward to someone in return for a service they provided or a work they finished.
to remunerate / to pay / to salary / to fee; Verb meaning to pay someone for the labor or time they spent working for you, usually used in a professional or business context.
to gratify / to reward / to bestow / to please; Verb meaning to give a person a reward or a favor to show your gratitude, or figuratively to satisfy a desire or a feeling.
to reward / to recompense / to prize / to compensate; Common verb meaning to give something good to someone because they worked hard, behaved well, or achieved something great.
to take precedence over / to award a prize to / to prime / to surpass; Verb with two meanings: to be more important than everything else, or to give an official prize to a winner in a competition.
to crown / to cap / to complete / to award the highest prize; Verb meaning to put a crown on a king's head, or figuratively to finish a long project with a final brilliant success or a top award.
to crown / to anoint / to swear / to curse; Verb meaning to officially name someone as king or champion in a religious ceremony, or informally (in Quebec) to use a swear word.
to vow / to dedicate / to devote / to doom; Verb meaning to promise your life or a specific effort to a person or a cause, or to doom someone to a bad fate (like failure).
to devote oneself / to sacrifice oneself / to dedicate oneself; Pronominal verb meaning to give all your time, energy, and love to help another person or to make a project succeed.

to sacrifice / to give up / to offer up / to immolate; Verb meaning to kill an animal for a god, or figuratively to give up something very precious (like sleep or money) to get something more important.
to immolate / to sacrifice / to offer as a victim / to burn (oneself); Formal verb meaning to kill a living being as a religious offering, or to kill oneself (often by fire) as a political protest.
to dedicate / to devote / to consecrate / to sanctify; Verb meaning to officially name a monument, a church, or a book in honor of a person, or to spend all your time on a specific task.
to dedicate (a book) / to sign / to autograph / to inscribe; Verb meaning to write a short personal message and your signature on the first page of a book or on a photo for a fan or a friend.
to initial / to sign / to sign off on / to endorse; Verb meaning to put your initials (the first letters of your name) on every page of a legal contract to show that you have read and accepted it.
to ratify / to confirm / to approve / to sanction; Formal verb meaning for a government or an organization to officially approve a treaty or an agreement that was already signed by representatives.

to validate / to confirm / to authenticate / to stamp (a ticket); Verb meaning to make something legally valid, or to check that a computer password is correct, or to put a ticket into a machine at the station.
to ratify / to confirm / to endorse / to make final; Formal verb meaning to officially accept a decision or a law that was made previously, making it permanent and final.
to legitimize / to justify / to recognize / to make lawful; Verb meaning to prove that an action is fair and right, or to officially recognize a child as a legal heir.
to motivate / to justify / to give reasons for / to inspire; Verb meaning to give the logical reasons for a decision, or to make someone feel excited and eager to work hard.
to argue / to make a case / to reason / to provide arguments; Verb meaning to give several logical reasons to support your opinion and to try to convince someone else that you are right.
to debate / to discuss / to argue / to struggle; Verb meaning to discuss an important subject in a formal meeting where people have different opinions, or to struggle physically against a danger.
to dialogue / to converse / to talk / to communicate; Verb meaning for two people or two groups to have a serious and calm conversation to understand each other or to solve a problem.
to confer / to bestow / to consult / to compare; Verb meaning to give a title or a prize to someone, or to have a meeting with colleagues to share opinions before making a decision.
to negotiate / to trade / to bargain / to clear (an obstacle); Verb meaning to discuss terms of a contract or a peace treaty, or to successfully move past a difficult turn in the road or a fence.
to haggle / to bargain / to be stingy / to spare; Verb meaning to try to get a lower price when buying something, or figuratively to refuse to give enough effort or time to a task.
to traffic / to tamper with / to trade / to fiddle with; Verb meaning to engage in illegal trade (like drugs), or to secretly change a machine or a document to trick someone.
to falsify / to forge / to tamper with / to doctor; Verb meaning to change a document, a signature, or a scientific result on purpose to trick people or to win a case illegally.
to rig / to doctor / to fake / to stack (the deck); Verb meaning to use secret tricks to change the result of a game, an election, or a photo so that it shows something that isn't real.
to make up / to disguise / to paint (the face) / to mask; Verb meaning to put paint, fake beards, or makeup on an actor's face so they look like someone else or like a monster.
to disguise / to conceal / to mask / to dress up; Verb meaning to change your appearance using clothes or a mask so people don't recognize you, or to hide your true feelings behind nice words.

to misrepresent / to travesty / to disguise / to distort (facts); Verb meaning to describe a situation or a speech in a very dishonest way that makes it look ridiculous or wrong, or to dress up as someone of the opposite gender.

to distort / to denature / to misrepresent / to spoil (the essence); Verb meaning to change the natural quality of a substance, or to change the meaning of a story so much that it is no longer true to the original.
to alter / to spoil / to distort / to make thirsty; Verb meaning to change something in a way that makes it worse or less pure, or for a physical condition (like heat) to make someone very thirsty.
to distort / to warp / to falsify / to throw off; Verb meaning to bend a metal object out of shape, to sing out of tune, or to give false information that makes a calculation wrong.
to slant / to skew / to bias / to use shifts / to dodge; Verb meaning to move in a diagonal direction, or figuratively to avoid answering a question directly by using clever and dishonest talk.
to influence / to bend / to sway / to change the course; Verb meaning to change the direction of a line slightly, or to influence a decision or a policy so it becomes different from what was planned.
to influence / to sway / to bias / to affect; Common verb meaning to have an effect on the way someone thinks or behaves, often through power, money, or a strong personality.

to suggest / to influence by suggestion / to hypnotize / to put ideas into someone's head; Verb meaning to use psychological power or repeated words to make someone believe or do something without them realizing it is your idea.
to manipulate / to handle / to rig / to control (people); Verb meaning to handle an object with your hands, or to use dishonest methods to control people's opinions or to change a machine's result.
to intrigue / to plot / to scheme / to puzzle / to fascinate; Verb meaning to secretly plan something against someone, or for a mystery to make someone very curious and interested to find the answer.
to plot / to conspire / to scheme / to hatch a plot; Verb meaning for several people to secretly work together to do something illegal or to hurt someone in a high position, like a king.

to conspire / to plot / to work together (for a result) / to unite; Verb meaning to secretly plan a bad action with others, or for several natural events to happen together to produce a specific (often bad) result.

to get along / to reach an agreement / to hear each other / to be understood; Pronominal verb meaning for two people to have a friendly relationship, or for a group to successfully reach a shared decision after a discussion.

to agree / to match / to grant each other / to harmonize; Pronominal verb meaning for colors or ideas to look/sound good together, or for two people to give each other a specific right or a moment of time.
to sympathize / to get along / to hit it off / to feel for; Verb meaning to quickly feel a friendly connection with a new person because you share the same tastes or the same way of thinking.

to fraternize / to associate as brothers / to be friendly (with an enemy); Verb meaning to treat someone like a brother, or for soldiers from two enemy armies to stop fighting and talk to each other in a friendly way.

to reconcile / to make up / to become friends again / to harmonize; Pronominal verb meaning to become friends again after a fight or a long period of silence, or to make two opposing ideas work together.
to absolve / to acquit / to forgive (sins) / to exonerate; Formal verb meaning for a priest to forgive someone's sins, or for a judge to state that a person is not guilty of a crime.
to amnesty / to pardon / to grant an amnesty to; Official verb meaning for a government to stop punishing a whole group of people for past political crimes and to erase their record.

to pardon (by a head of state) / to show mercy to / to spare; Verb meaning for a president or a king to decide that a criminal will not be punished (especially avoiding the death penalty) as a special act of mercy.
to release / to acquit (legal) / to relax / to loosen; Verb with two meanings: for a court to release a suspect because there is not enough proof, or to rest your body and mind to reduce stress.

to widen / to release (a prisoner) / to broaden / to extend; Verb meaning to make a hole or a road bigger, or figuratively for a court to let a prisoner go out of jail (putting them back into the wide world).
to release / to loosen / to let go / to slacken; Verb meaning to let a prisoner go, to stop holding a rope tightly, or for a person to stop working so hard and become lazy.
to exonerate / to exempt / to free from (taxes) / to discharge; Formal verb meaning to state that someone is not responsible for a debt or a crime, or to allow them to not pay a specific tax.
