to lament / to wail / to moan / to complain loudly; Verb meaning to express a deep and loud sorrow through cries and words, often because of a death or a great misfortune.
to complain / to groan / to grumble / to lodge a complaint; Verb meaning to express pain, dissatisfaction, or a feeling of being treated unfairly, either through words or by a formal legal action.
to cry out / to exclaim / to protest / to shout in surprise; Verb meaning to suddenly and loudly express surprise, admiration, or a strong protest against something that was just said or seen.
to jeer / to mock / to scoff / to poke fun at; Literary verb meaning to laugh at someone or something in a mocking and superior way, making them look ridiculous.
to mock / to make fun of / to not care about / to delude oneself; Verb meaning to laugh at a person to be mean or funny, or to consider a rule or a danger as not important at all.
to mock / to jeer / to taunt / to banter; Verb meaning to attack someone with sharp and witty jokes, or to make fun of their appearance or their failures in a slightly cruel way.
to get angry / to fall out / to be annoyed / to take offense; Verb meaning to start feeling a strong displeasure against someone, or for two friends to stop speaking to each other because of a fight.

to lose one's temper / to fly into a rage / to be carried away / to be easily moved; Verb meaning to suddenly and violently lose control of your speech and actions because of an explosion of anger, or to be physically carried away by a fast horse or a flood.
to rush / to dash / to charge / to kick out (horse); Verb meaning to move very fast and with a lot of force towards a person, a place, or a goal, or for an animal to kick with its back legs.

to spring / to dash / to soar / to throb (pain); Verb meaning to start a fast movement with energy (like starting a race or a plane taking off), or for a part of the body to feel a sharp, rhythmic pain.

to rush / to hurry / to hurl oneself / to precipitate (chemistry); Verb meaning to act or move very quickly without thinking carefully, or to physically jump or fall from a height, or for a substance to fall as a solid in a liquid.
to hasten / to hurry / to make haste / to speed up; Formal verb meaning to do something as quickly as possible or to go somewhere fast because you don't have much time.
to hasten / to be eager to / to hurry / to bustle about; Verb meaning to show a lot of speed and energy in doing something because you are very eager to help or to get a result.
to hurry up / to make haste / to look sharp / to get a move on; Common verb meaning to do an action or to go to a place faster than normal because you are late or in a rush.
to hurry / to press against each other / to crowd / to squeeze; Verb meaning to act quickly or to be in a place where people are pushing against you, or to squeeze a fruit to get the juice.
to jostle / to push each other / to bustle / to rush (things); Verb meaning for people to push each other in a crowd, or to do tasks too quickly and in a disorganized way.

to collide / to bump into / to clash / to encounter (difficulty); Verb meaning to physically hit an object or a person while moving, or figuratively to meet a problem or an opposition that stops your progress.
to bang / to knock (oneself) / to bump / to fight (slang); Verb meaning to accidentally hit a part of your body against a hard object (like a door or a table), often causing a bruise.
to hurt oneself / to be injured / to wound / to offend (someone); Verb meaning to cause physical damage to your own body, or figuratively to hurt someone's feelings or pride.

to cut oneself / to intersect / to interrupt oneself / to be cut off; Verb meaning to make a wound in your skin with a sharp tool like a knife, or for two roads to cross each other, or to stop speaking suddenly.

to burn oneself / to get burnt / to ruin (one's chances) / to skip (a red light); Verb meaning to hurt your skin with fire or something very hot, or figuratively to lose your reputation or chances of success by doing something wrong.

to prick oneself / to take pride (rarely) / to inject oneself / to be offended; Verb meaning to make a small hole in your skin with a needle or a thorn, or to inject a drug, or rarely to feel proud about a quality.
to twist / to wring / to double up (laughing) / to sprain; Verb meaning to move your body or a limb out of its natural shape, or to laugh so much that your body bends, or to sprain an ankle.

to straighten up / to stand up straight / to recover / to right itself; Verb meaning to move from a bent or slumping position to a straight, vertical one, or figuratively for a business or a situation to start improving after a bad period.

to lean / to bend / to look into / to study (a problem); Verb meaning to move the top part of the body forward and down, or figuratively to spend time studying or thinking about a specific subject or problem.
to bow / to tilt / to lean / to yield; Verb meaning to bend the head or body as a sign of respect or greeting, or for an object to be at an angle, or to accept a decision or a defeat.
to bend / to bow / to stoop / to humble oneself; Verb meaning to curve the back or the whole body downwards, often because of heavy work, old age, or because you are being very submissive to someone.

to sag / to collapse / to sink / to slump down; Verb meaning for a structure to slowly sink or for a person to suddenly lose strength and fall into a sitting or lying position because of tiredness or shock.

to collapse / to fall down / to crumble / to break down (crying); Verb meaning for a large building or a system to fall down suddenly and violently, or for a person to suddenly start crying because they can no longer control their grief.

to collapse / to cave in / to break down (crying) / to plummet (prices); Verb meaning for a floor or a roof to fall in, or for a person to lose all psychological strength, or for prices and values to fall very quickly.
to faint / to vanish / to disappear / to fade away; Verb meaning to lose consciousness for a short time, or for a sound, a smell, or a ghost to gradually become invisible and disappear completely.

to dissipate / to vanish / to clear up / to waste (time/money); Verb meaning for clouds, fog, or a feeling (like doubt) to break up and disappear, or for a person to spend their resources in a foolish way.

to volatilize / to vanish / to disappear into thin air / to evaporate; Verb meaning for a liquid to turn into gas, or figuratively for a person or an object (like stolen money) to disappear so suddenly that no trace is left.
to evaporate / to vanish / to disappear / to waste away; Verb meaning for a liquid to change into vapor because of heat, or for a hope or a memory to slowly go away until nothing is left.

to condense / to thicken / to summarize / to concentrate; Verb meaning for gas to turn into liquid (like steam into water on a window), or to make a long book or a speech much shorter by keeping only the main points.

to liquefy / to melt / to become liquid / to dissolve; Verb meaning for a solid or a gas to turn into a liquid state, often through heat or pressure, or figuratively for a person to lose their courage and become weak.

to solidify / to set / to harden / to become firm; Verb meaning for a liquid to turn into a solid (like water into ice), or figuratively for a plan, a project, or a friendship to become stronger and more definite.

to crystallize / to take shape / to become clear / to set; Verb meaning for a substance to form crystals, or figuratively for a vague idea or a feeling to suddenly become very clear, fixed, and definite in the mind.

to stabilize / to become steady / to level off / to settle down; Verb meaning for a situation, a price, or a person's health to stop changing and become firm and steady after a period of movement or crisis.
to balance (oneself/each other) / to reach equilibrium / to offset; Verb meaning for two opposing forces or weights to become equal so that everything remains stable and does not fall or fail.

to swing / to rock / to balance / to not care (slang); Verb meaning to move back and forth on a swing or a chair, or to walk with a rhythmic sway, or slangly to express that you don't care at all about something.

to shake / to wave / to fidget / to be restless; Verb meaning to move your body or a part of it quickly and constantly, often because of nervousness, anger, or excitement, or for a liquid to be stirred.
to wriggle / to dance about / to fidget / to shake one's hips; Informal verb meaning to move the body with small, quick, and rhythmic movements, often while dancing or because of a happy impatience.
to wriggle / to twist / to squirm / to shuffle; Verb meaning to move the body or an object by twisting it many times, often because of physical pain, embarrassment, or being uncomfortable.
to struggle / to wrestle / to thrash about / to try hard; Verb meaning to move the limbs violently to escape from a person holding you or from a difficult situation like drowning or a trap.

to revolt / to rebel / to be disgusted / to rise up; Verb meaning to refuse to obey an authority or a government and take action against it, or to feel a strong sense of moral disgust towards an injustice.
to rebel / to mutiny / to resist / to be defiant; Verb meaning to openly resist an established government or a person in power, often used for soldiers or children who refuse to follow rules.
to rise up / to rebel / to protest / to take a stand; Formal verb meaning to formally and strongly protest against an idea or a law, or for a large group of people to start an insurrection.

to rise up / to heave / to feel sick / to be lifted; Verb meaning for a group to start a revolution, or for the chest to move up and down heavily while breathing, or for the stomach to feel like you are about to vomit.

to rear up (horse) / to bristle / to dig in one's heels / to rebel; Verb meaning for a horse to stand on its back legs because of fear or anger, or figuratively for a person to refuse to do something very stubbornly.
to charge / to dash / to darken / to pounce; Verb meaning to move at high speed towards a target without hesitation, or for a color to become darker and more intense.
to leap / to spring / to bounce / to jump up; Verb meaning to move suddenly and quickly by jumping (like a lion attacking or a ball hitting the ground and coming back up).
to fly away / to take flight / to disappear / to vanish; Verb meaning for a bird or a plane to leave the ground and start flying, or figuratively for hope or time to disappear very quickly.

to frolic / to gambol / to romp / to play about; Verb meaning for animals or children to move around in a happy, lively way, often in an open space like a field or a park, because they feel free and energetic.

to enjoy oneself / to have fun / to amuse oneself / to turn away (funds); Verb meaning to spend time doing things that make you happy and relaxed (like a hobby or a show), or in a legal sense, to move money from its intended place.
to have fun / to enjoy oneself / to play / to laugh at (someone); Common verb meaning to do something that gives you pleasure or makes you laugh, or to spend time playing with toys or games.

to distract oneself / to enjoy oneself / to relax / to be absent-minded; Verb meaning to do something light and pleasant to forget about your work or your worries for a while, or to fail to pay attention to something.
to relax / to unwind / to rest / to ease up; Verb meaning to get rid of physical or mental tiredness by doing something calm and pleasant (like a warm bath or reading).
to relax / to loosen up / to unwind / to slacken; Verb meaning for a muscle or a rope to become less tight, or figuratively for a person to become calm and free from stress or worry.
to rest / to rely (on) / to lie (down) / to settle; Verb meaning to stop working or moving so that you can get your strength back, or to trust someone completely, or for a dead body to be in a grave.

to doze off / to drift off / to become drowsy / to die down (fire); Verb meaning to fall into a light and short sleep, often while sitting or during the day, or for a feeling or a problem to become less intense.
to fall asleep / to go to sleep / to become numb / to grow dull; Verb meaning to pass from a conscious state to a state of sleep, or for a part of the body to lose feeling because of bad blood flow.
to wake up / to awaken / to come to life / to be aroused; Verb meaning to stop sleeping and become conscious again, or for a feeling like hunger or memories to start being active again.
to wake up / to awaken / to be aroused / to open up (flower); Formal verb meaning to wake up, or figuratively for a talent, a sense, or a plant to start growing or being active for the first time.
to get up / to stand up / to rise (sun) / to lift (fog); Verb meaning to move from a sitting or lying position to a standing one, or for the sun to appear in the morning, or for a storm to start.

to sit down / to be seated / to establish / to settle; Verb meaning to place your body on a chair or the ground so that your weight is on your buttocks, or figuratively to build a strong foundation for a project.
to squat / to crouch / to hunker down / to cower; Verb meaning to sit with your knees bent and your heels touching your buttocks, or to hide by making yourself very small near the ground.
to kneel down / to fall to one's knees / to submit / to bow down; Verb meaning to put one or both knees on the ground, often to show respect, to pray, or to look for something low down.
to prostrate / to bow down / to grovel / to submit humbly; Verb meaning to lie flat on the ground with the face down, or to kneel deeply as a sign of extreme respect or religious worship.

to get up again / to stand up again / to recover / to pick oneself up; Verb meaning to move back to a standing position after falling or sitting, or figuratively to start succeeding again after a major failure or illness.

to sit down again / to be seated again / to settle back down / to calm down; Verb meaning to return to a sitting position after having stood up, or figuratively for a liquid or a situation to become calm and clear again.
to go back to bed / to lie down again / to set again (star); Verb meaning to return to bed to sleep more after having woken up or gotten up for a short time.
to fall asleep again / to drift back to sleep / to go back to sleep; Verb meaning to pass into a state of sleep for a second time after an interruption during the night or the morning.

to shake oneself / to snort (horse) / to wake up briskly / to splash around; Verb meaning to shake the whole body to get rid of water or dust, or for a horse to breathe out loudly through the nose, or figuratively to wake up and get active quickly.

to shower / to have a shower / to dampen (enthusiasm) / to drench; Verb meaning to wash the body under a spray of water, or figuratively to suddenly stop someone's joy or energy by giving them bad news.
to bathe / to swim / to soak / to be immersed in; Verb meaning to enter water (a tub, a pool, or the sea) to wash or to have fun, or figuratively to be completely surrounded by light or blood.

to wash (oneself) / to clean oneself / to clear (one's name) / to be washed; Common verb meaning to make yourself clean using water and soap, or figuratively to prove that you are not guilty of a crime.
to soap (oneself) / to lather up / to rub with soap / to reprimand (rarely); Verb meaning to cover the body or a part of it with soap or lather before rinsing it with water.

to rinse (oneself/one's mouth) / to wash off / to clear out / to feast (one's eyes); Verb meaning to clean soap or dirt off with pure water, or to wash the inside of the mouth, or figuratively to enjoy looking at something beautiful.

to dry (oneself) / to dry up / to wither / to skip (class); Verb meaning to remove water from the body or an object (often using a towel or the sun), or figuratively to skip a school lesson without permission.

to wipe (oneself) / to dry / to suffer (a refusal/fire) / to undergo; Verb meaning to clean or dry something by rubbing it with a cloth or a tissue, or figuratively to experience an unpleasant event like a refusal or an attack.

to rub (oneself) / to scrub / to mix with / to clash with; Verb meaning to move your hand or a cloth back and forth on your skin, or figuratively to have contact with dangerous people or difficult problems.
to scratch (oneself) / to itch / to scrape / to play (guitar); Verb meaning to rub the skin with the fingernails because it itches, or to remove a layer of something with a sharp tool.

to blow one's nose / to snub (someone) / to trim (a candle); Verb meaning to push air out of the nose into a tissue to clean it, or figuratively to treat someone with contempt, or technically to cut the burnt part of a candle wick.

to scour / to clean out (ears/teeth) / to scrub / to pick (one's nose); Verb meaning to clean an object by rubbing it hard (like a pot), or to clean the inside of the ears or between the teeth using a small tool.

to brush (oneself/hair/teeth) / to go without (slang) / to paint (quickly); Verb meaning to use a brush on the hair, the teeth, or the clothes to make them clean or tidy, or slangly meaning to realize that you won't get something you wanted.
to comb one's hair / to tidy oneself / to be visible (rarely); Verb meaning to use a comb to disentangle and style the hair.

to do one's hair / to put on a hat / to outstrip / to be capped; Verb meaning to arrange the hair in a specific style, or to put a headcovering on, or figuratively to reach a goal just before someone else.

to shave / to be bored (slang) / to graze / to skim; Verb meaning to cut the hair of the face or body very close to the skin using a razor, or slangly to be extremely bored by a long and dull situation.
to epilate / to pluck (hair) / to remove body hair; Verb meaning to remove unwanted hair from the body by pulling it out from the roots, usually using wax or tweezers.

to put on makeup / to disguise / to falsify (documents) / to cheat; Verb meaning to apply cosmetic products to the face to change or improve its appearance, or figuratively to hide the truth or falsify a paper.

to put on makeup / to paint one's face / to disguise (one's feelings) / to blush (rarely); Literary verb meaning to apply heavy makeup or paint to the face, often used to hide age or to look like a performer, or figuratively to present something in a false way.
to remove makeup / to cleanse the face; Verb meaning to clean the cosmetic products off the face, usually before going to sleep.
to get dressed / to wear / to suit / to provide clothes; Verb meaning to put on clothes, or figuratively for a style or a color to look good on a person.
to dress oneself / to clothe oneself / to cover / to be dressed; Formal and literary verb meaning to put on garments or to cover the body for protection or modesty.
to get undressed / to take off clothes / to strip / to lay bare; Verb meaning to take off the clothes you are wearing, or figuratively to reveal the hidden truth about a person or a situation.
to undress / to strip / to take off garments / to divest (legal); Formal and literary verb meaning to remove one's clothing, or in a legal sense, to give up a right or a property.

to get dressed again / to be told off (slang) / to put clothes back on; Verb meaning to put your clothes back on after having taken them off, or slangly meaning to be sent away or criticized so harshly that you have nothing left to say.

to take off one's trousers / to back down (slang) / to cave in / to strip; Verb meaning to remove one's pants, or slangly to admit defeat or change one's opinion very quickly because of pressure or fear.
to put on one's shoes / to wear shoes / to fit (shoes) / to provide shoes; Verb meaning to put footwear on your feet, or to have a certain shoe size, or to provide shoes for someone.

to take off one's shoes / to lose one's teeth (gums) / to uncover roots / to slip off; Verb meaning to remove your shoes, or for the gums to move away from the teeth, or for soil to be removed from the roots of a tree.
to put on gloves / to wear gloves / to fit like a glove; Verb meaning to put gloves on the hands, or figuratively for a piece of clothing to fit the body perfectly.

to veil oneself / to be clouded / to buckle (wheel) / to hide; Verb meaning for a person to cover their face or head with a veil, or for the sun to be hidden by clouds, or for a flat object (like a wheel or a board) to become bent or twisted.
to unmask oneself / to reveal oneself / to be exposed / to take off a mask; Verb meaning to take off a mask, or figuratively to show your true character or intentions which were previously hidden.

to look at oneself in a mirror / to be reflected / to admire oneself / to examine (eggs); Verb meaning to see your own image in a mirror or in calm water, or figuratively to admire yourself too much, or technically to check eggs by holding them to the light.

to contemplate oneself / to gaze at oneself / to admire oneself / to reflect; Formal verb meaning to look at your own face or body with great attention and for a long time, often with a sense of pride or deep thought.

to admire oneself / to be admired / to think highly of oneself / to be wonderful; Verb meaning to look at oneself with pleasure and approval, or for a person or object to be the subject of someone else's admiration.

to flatter oneself / to boast / to hope / to stroke (oneself); Verb meaning to believe you have qualities that you might not really have, or to boast about something, or to gently rub a part of your body.
to boast / to brag / to pride oneself on / to claim; Common verb meaning to speak with too much pride about your own achievements, possessions, or abilities.
to pride oneself / to boast / to take credit / to be glorified; Formal and religious verb meaning to show great pride in something you have done, or for a person to be honored and praised.
to pride oneself / to take pride / to be proud / to become arrogant; High formal verb meaning to feel a strong sense of satisfaction and pride because of a quality or a victory.

to prick oneself / to pride oneself / to take a hit (drugs) / to turn sour (wine); Verb meaning to accidentally hurt the skin with a needle or a thorn, or figuratively to take great pride in a specific skill, or slangly to inject drugs.
to get angry / to fall out / to take offense / to become cross; Common verb meaning to feel and show anger towards someone, or for two friends to stop speaking to each other after an argument.
to get angry / to fly into a rage / to lose one's cool / to blow up; Verb phrase meaning to experience and show a strong feeling of displeasure and hostility towards someone or something.

to lose one's temper / to fly into a rage / to be carried away / to bolt (horse); Verb meaning to suddenly become very angry and start speaking or acting without control, or for a horse to run away because it is frightened.
to get irritated / to get worked up / to get annoyed / to lose one's nerves; Common verb meaning to become increasingly annoyed or nervous about something that is happening slowly or repeatedly.
to get irritated / to become annoyed / to be sore / to chafe; Verb meaning for the skin or a part of the body to become red and painful, or figuratively for a person to feel a mild but growing anger.

to get exasperated / to become intensely annoyed / to worsen (illness); Verb meaning to reach a point where you have no more patience left and feel a very strong irritation, or for a medical condition to become more serious.
to be indignant / to be outraged / to protest / to be shocked; Verb meaning to feel a strong and righteous anger because of an injustice, a lie, or an unfair action.
to be scandalized / to be shocked / to take offense / to be horrified; Verb meaning to be deeply shocked and offended by a behavior or a word that goes against morality or religion.
to take offense / to be offended / to be shadowed / to be obscured; Verb meaning to feel hurt or insulted by a remark or a situation, or for light to be blocked by an object.

to take offense / to be offended / to get crumpled / to be bruised; Verb meaning for clothes or paper to lose their smooth surface, or figuratively for a person to feel a slight but painful blow to their pride.
to take offense / to be hurt / to be upset / to be annoyed; Common verb meaning to feel slight anger and sadness because someone has said something that you think is critical or mocking.

to take offense / to take exception / to be stickler for rules / to be formal; Verb meaning to feel offended because someone has failed to follow the proper social rules or etiquette, or to insist on following those rules strictly.
to reconcile / to make up / to be consistent / to harmonize; Verb meaning for two people to become friends again after an argument, or for two ideas or accounts to be brought into agreement.
to make up / to reconcile / to be mended / to be repaired; Informal verb meaning to become friends again after a fight, or for a piece of clothing to be fixed by sewing.

to fall out / to become blurred / to become confused / to be scrambled (eggs); Verb meaning for two people to have an argument and stop being friends, or for the vision to become unclear, or for thoughts to become mixed up.
to argue / to quarrel / to compete for / to contest; Common verb meaning to have an angry disagreement using words, or to fight with others to get a prize or a position.
to quarrel / to bicker / to squabble / to dispute; Verb meaning to have a loud and angry disagreement about small or unimportant things, often used for siblings or neighbors.
to fight / to scuffle / to brawl / to scrap; Informal verb meaning to engage in a physical fight, usually without weapons, involving hitting or pushing.

to fight / to struggle / to combat / to flap (wings); Common verb meaning to use physical force or weapons against an enemy, or figuratively to make a great effort to achieve something difficult or to survive.
to face each other / to clash / to confront each other / to oppose; Verb meaning for two people, armies, or teams to meet and fight or compete against each other to see who is stronger.
to collide / to bump into / to clash / to come up against; Verb meaning to accidentally hit an object or a person while moving, or figuratively to have a strong disagreement with an idea or a rule.
to bang / to hit (oneself) / to bump into / to slog away (slang); Verb meaning to hit a part of your body against a hard surface by accident, or slangly to have to do a long and difficult job.

to collide (cars) / to not care (slang) / to dab / to buffer; Verb meaning for two vehicles to hit each other, or to gently touch a wound with a piece of cotton, or slangly (with 'de') to not care about something at all.
to collide / to crash into / to strike / to understand (slang); Verb meaning for two moving objects to hit each other with great force, or slangly to suddenly understand something.

to crash / to be crushed / to shut up (slang) / to flatten itself; Verb meaning for a plane or car to hit the ground or a wall and be destroyed, or to be pressed so hard that the shape is ruined, or slangly to stop talking or protesting.
to flatten / to grovel / to kowtow / to become flat; Verb meaning to become flat or thin, or figuratively to behave in a very humble or weak way before someone powerful to get a favor.

to spread (out) / to fall flat / to show off / to be spaced out; Verb meaning to cover a surface with a layer of something, or to fall down at full length on the ground, or to talk too much about your own success.
to spread / to spill / to overflow / to be rumored; Verb meaning for a liquid to flow out of a container, or for a smell, a light, or a news story to become known in many places.
to spread / to propagate / to be transmitted / to increase; Verb meaning for a disease, a fire, or a wave to move from one point to another, or for a plant or animal to reproduce.
to spread / to be broadcast / to diffuse / to permeate; Verb meaning for a light or a smell to fill a space softly, or for a radio or TV program to be sent to many people.

to scatter / to disperse / to be distracted / to waste one's energy; Verb meaning for objects to be thrown in different directions, or figuratively for a person to try to do too many things at once and lose focus.
to bicker / to squabble / to tiff / to wrangle; Informal verb meaning to have a small and noisy argument, especially between children or close friends, about things that are not very important.
to scold / to mob / to nag / to pull about; Verb meaning to criticize someone harshly or repeatedly, or to pull someone around roughly in a game or a crowd.

to make fun of / to mock / to laugh at / to not care (with 'de'); Common verb meaning to laugh at someone in an unkind way to make them look stupid, or (with 'de') to show that you think something is not important at all.

to laugh at / to make light of / to defy / to play with; Literary verb phrase (followed by 'de') meaning to treat a danger or a difficulty as if it were funny or unimportant, or to mock someone's feelings.
to mock / to jeer / to scoff at / to banter; Literary and formal verb meaning to express contempt or ridicule for someone or their ideas using clever or sharp words.
to poke fun at / to mock / to jeer / to ridicule; Literary and somewhat old-fashioned verb meaning to mock someone or something openly and often with a sense of superiority.
to laugh one's head off / to split one's sides laughing (slang) / to have a good laugh; Slang verb meaning to laugh extremely hard, usually because something is very funny or ridiculous.
to laugh / to have a laugh (slang) / to have fun / to enjoy oneself; Common slang verb meaning to have a good time or to find something funny.
to have fun / to enjoy oneself / to play / to dally; Common verb meaning to spend time doing things that make you happy and relaxed, or to play with an object or a thought.
to enjoy oneself / to have fun / to be entertained / to deviate; Formal verb meaning to find pleasure in an activity or show, or technically to turn someone's attention away from a path or a duty.

to rejoice / to be glad / to be delighted / to look forward to; Formal verb meaning to feel and show great happiness about a piece of news or a victory, or to feel happy in advance about a future event.
to congratulate oneself / to be pleased / to rejoice / to praise oneself; Verb meaning to feel satisfied with your own actions or a situation, or to express happiness about a good result.
to congratulate oneself / to applaud oneself / to be proud / to rejoice; Literary verb phrase meaning to feel very happy and proud of yourself for having done something smart or successful.

to boast / to pride oneself / to claim / to brag; Formal verb (followed by 'de') meaning to speak with pride about a quality or a skill that you believe you have, often used when the speaker is a bit skeptical.
to take advantage of / to pride oneself / to avail oneself / to rely on; Formal verb (followed by 'de') meaning to use a fact, a right, or a quality to your advantage or to show your importance.

to lean / to rely on / to be based on / to rest on; Verb meaning to put your weight on something to stay steady, or figuratively to use facts or someone's help as the basis for your work or your confidence.
to lean one's elbows / to rest on one's elbows / to lean over; Verb meaning to put your elbows on a table, a railing, or a window sill to support the upper body.
to lean / to bend / to look into / to take an interest in; Verb meaning to move the top part of the body forward or to one side, or (with 'sur') to examine a problem or a situation carefully.

to bow / to lean / to tilt / to yield / to slope; Verb meaning to bend the head or body as a sign of respect, or for a surface to not be level, or figuratively to accept a decision or an authority after a fight.

to bend / to bow / to stoop / to humble oneself; Verb meaning to change shape from straight to a curve, or for a person to lower their body because of age, weight, or to show extreme respect/submission.
to fold / to bend / to comply / to submit; Verb meaning for an object (like paper or cloth) to be doubled over, or figuratively to follow a rule or a command even if you don't want to.

to twist / to wring / to writhe / to sprain; Verb meaning to turn part of the body or an object in a different direction, or to move the body violently because of pain or laughter ('se tordre de rire'), or to injure a joint.

to stand up straight / to straighten up / to recover / to right itself; Verb meaning to return to a vertical position after being bent or lying down, or for a situation (like the economy) to start improving after a bad period.

to stand up / to rise / to be erected / to be trained (animal); Verb meaning to move into a vertical position, or for a large building or mountain to appear high in the distance, or for an animal to be taught to obey.

to get up / to rise / to stand up / to clear up (weather); Common verb meaning to leave your bed after sleeping, or to stand up from a sitting position, or for the sun to appear in the morning, or for the wind to start blowing.
to wake up / to awaken / to be revived / to start again; Common verb meaning to stop sleeping and become conscious, or figuratively for a feeling or a memory to become strong again.
to wake up / to awaken (formal/metaphorical) / to be born / to sprout; Formal verb meaning to become awake, or figuratively for an interest, a talent, or a nature-process to begin for the first time.

to fall asleep / to go to sleep / to grow numb / to be neglected; Verb meaning to start sleeping, or for a part of the body to lose feeling (pins and needles), or for a project to stop moving forward.
to fall back asleep / to go back to sleep; Verb meaning to go back to a state of sleep after having been awake for a short time.
to go to bed / to lie down / to set (sun) / to be written down; Common verb meaning to get into bed to sleep, or to put your body in a horizontal position, or for the sun to disappear at night.
to sit down at the table / to sit down to a meal; Verb meaning to take a seat at a table, usually with other people, for the purpose of eating a meal or having a discussion.

to sit down / to take a seat / to be based on / to settle; Common verb meaning to lower your body onto a chair, the ground, or another surface, or figuratively for a reputation or a power to be firmly established.

to station oneself / to post oneself / to take up a position / to wait; Verb meaning to choose a specific place to stand and stay there, usually to watch something, to wait for someone, or to perform a duty (like a soldier or a guard).

to place oneself / to get a job / to take a position / to invest (money); Verb meaning to put yourself in a specific spot, or to find a professional position for yourself, or to put money into a bank or stock to earn interest.

to settle in / to install oneself / to set up / to sit down comfortably; Verb meaning to move into a new house or office and arrange your things, or to put yourself in a comfortable position to stay for a while.
to settle / to establish oneself / to set up business / to be proven; Formal verb meaning to choose a place to live or work permanently, or for a fact or a rule to be officially accepted as true.
to settle down / to stare / to fix oneself / to decide; Verb meaning to stop moving from place to place and choose a permanent home, or to look at someone intensely, or to decide on a date or a goal.

to anchor oneself / to take root / to be firmly fixed / to be ingrained; Verb meaning for a boat to stop using an anchor, or figuratively for a habit, a belief, or a person to become so firmly part of a place or a mind that it is hard to remove.

to establish oneself / to take root / to be implanted / to expand (business); Verb meaning for a company to open branches in a new region, or for a habit or a biological organ to be successfully put into place and start functioning.

to take root / to become rooted / to be deep-seated / to settle; Verb meaning for a plant to grow roots into the ground, or figuratively for a custom, a prejudice, or a feeling to become so deep that it becomes a permanent part of a society or a person.

to stabilize / to become steady / to level off / to balance; Verb meaning to stop changing or moving and stay in a steady and balanced state, often used for prices, the weather, or a patient's health.

to balance oneself / to reach equilibrium / to offset / to compensate; Verb meaning for different forces or amounts to become equal and steady, or for a person to keep their body steady to avoid falling.
to adjust / to fit / to trim oneself / to aim (weapon); Verb meaning to make small changes to clothing or a tool to make it fit or work better, or to aim a weapon precisely at a target.

to be settled / to adjust oneself / to follow a rule / to be paid; Verb meaning for a problem or a bill to be finished and resolved, or for a machine to be put in perfect order, or to live according to a strict schedule.
to adapt / to fit / to adjust / to accommodate; Verb meaning to change your behavior or your ideas to suit a new situation, or for an object to be modified for a different use.

to get used to / to accustom oneself / to familiarize / to season; Formal verb (followed by 'à') meaning to gradually become familiar with a new situation, a climate, or a sound so that it no longer feels strange or difficult.
to get used to / to become accustomed / to develop a habit / to acclimatize; Common verb (followed by 'à') meaning to learn to live with something or do something regularly so that it feels normal.

to familiarize oneself / to get acquainted with / to master / to become comfortable; Verb (followed by 'avec') meaning to learn about a subject or a tool so that you understand it well and feel comfortable using it.
to submit / to yield / to comply / to undergo; Verb meaning to accept the power or the rules of someone else, or to offer a piece of work for judgment, or to experience a medical test.
to comply / to conform / to follow / to abide by; Verb (followed by 'à') meaning to act in agreement with a rule, a law, or an order, or to make your behavior similar to what is expected.

to pull over / to step aside / to range oneself / to settle down; Verb meaning to move your car or body out of the way of others, or figuratively for a wild person to start living a quiet and responsible life.

to rally / to join / to come round to / to regroup; Verb meaning to join a group or a political party, or to change your opinion to agree with someone else, or for soldiers to gather again after being scattered.
to join / to be joined / to associate with / to participate; Verb (followed by 'à') meaning to become a member of a group or to go somewhere with someone, or for two objects to be connected together.
to partner / to associate / to join forces / to be linked; Verb meaning to work together with someone in a business or a project, or for two ideas to be connected in the mind.

to bond / to link / to be tied / to make friends; Verb (often followed by 'à' or 'avec') meaning to form a strong relationship or a friendship with someone, or for two chemicals or elements to combine.
to get married / to wed / to match / to blend; Verb meaning to take someone as a husband or wife in a legal ceremony, or figuratively for colors or flavors to look or taste very good together.
to unite / to join together / to combine / to merge; Verb meaning for people, groups, or countries to act together to achieve a common goal, or for two elements to be physically joined into one.

to reconcile / to make up / to harmonize / to resolve a conflict; Verb meaning to become friends again after an argument or a fight, or to find a way to make two different ideas or facts exist together.

to get closer / to move closer / to approach / to look like (with 'de'); Verb meaning to reduce the distance between yourself and an object or a person, or for a date or an event to be coming soon, or to start being friends with someone again.

to meet (up) / to join / to agree / to catch up; Verb meaning to go to a place to find someone who is already there, or for two roads or rivers to meet, or for two people to have the same opinion about something.

to find oneself / to meet up / to turn up / to end up; Common verb meaning to find your way again after being lost, or to meet someone as planned, or to find yourself in a specific situation or place after some time.
to assemble / to gather / to be joined / to fit together; Verb meaning for people to come together in one place, or for pieces of a machine or a puzzle to be put together into one whole.

to meet / to gather / to reunite / to combine; Common verb meaning for a group of people to come together for a meeting, a party, or after a long time apart, or for different qualities to exist in one person.

to group together / to cluster / to band together / to categorize oneself; Verb meaning for people or things to arrange themselves into small groups or to stay close together for protection or a common purpose.
to gather in a crowd / to flock / to swarm / to mob; Verb meaning for a large and often noisy number of people to gather suddenly in a public place, often out of curiosity or to protest.
to push / to jostle / to rush / to hustle; Verb meaning to push people around in a crowd to move faster, or for thoughts and events to happen so quickly that they seem to collide in the mind.
to pile up / to huddle / to squeeze together / to cram; Verb meaning to be put or to put oneself in a very small space with many others, often in a disorganized or uncomfortable way.
to accumulate / to build up / to amass / to collect; Verb meaning for things (like work, money, or clouds) to increase in amount or number over a period of time.
to multiply / to increase / to reproduce / to manifold; Verb meaning to increase greatly in number or frequency, or for animals and plants to produce young.
to increase / to grow / to augment / to swell; Formal verb meaning to become greater in size, amount, degree, or power.
to develop / to grow / to expand / to be explained; Common verb meaning to grow and become more advanced or stronger, or for an idea to be explained in more detail, or for a film to be processed.

to bloom / to blossom / to flourish / to open up; Verb meaning for a flower to open its petals, or figuratively for a person to reach their full potential and feel happy and satisfied with their life.
to transform / to change / to turn into / to be converted; Verb (followed by 'en') meaning to change completely in form, appearance, or character.
to change / to be modified / to adjust / to be altered; Verb meaning to undergo small changes, usually to become better or to adapt to a new rule or situation.
to change / to deteriorate / to be distorted / to be thirsty (old); Verb meaning to change in a bad way (like food rotting or a voice shaking with emotion), or for a surface to be damaged by weather.
to prove to be / to turn out to be / to be found to be; Verb meaning to be recognized or discovered as being true or having a certain quality after an investigation or a period of time.
to reveal itself / to turn out to be / to be revealed / to show talent; Verb meaning for a fact or a secret to become known, or for a person to show a hidden quality or talent to the world.

to manifest oneself / to show oneself / to demonstrate / to break out (disease); Verb meaning to make one's presence or feelings known through actions or signs, or for a large group of people to protest in the streets.
to happen / to occur / to perform / to produce oneself; Verb meaning for an event to take place, or for an artist to give a performance in front of an audience, or to present oneself in a place.

to happen / to go / to take place / to do without (with 'de'); Very common verb meaning for an event to occur, or to describe how something is progressing, or (with 'de') to manage to live or work without something.

to take place / to unfold / to unroll / to proceed; Verb meaning for a ceremony, a match, or a story to take place over a period of time in a specific order, or for an object like a carpet to be unrolled.
to take place / to be carried out / to be operated on / to be effected; Formal verb meaning for a change or a process to happen, or for a patient to receive medical surgery.
to be fulfilled / to be accomplished / to take place / to complete itself; Formal verb meaning for a prophecy, a task, or a duty to be successfully completed or to come true.

to come true / to be fulfilled / to realize oneself / to understand (rare/Anglicism); Verb meaning for a dream or a project to become real, or for a person to reach their goals and feel satisfied with their life.
to be carried out / to take place / to be performed / to be made; Administrative and technical verb meaning for a task, a payment, or a movement to be completed or executed.
to materialize / to take shape / to be realized / to become concrete; Verb meaning for an abstract idea or a vague plan to finally become something real and visible.
to materialize / to take shape / to appear / to be embodied; Verb meaning to become a physical object, or for a spirit or a thought to appear in the real world.
to translate / to result in / to manifest itself / to be expressed; Verb (followed by 'par') meaning for a situation or a feeling to show itself through a specific result or action.
to express oneself / to be expressed / to speak out / to show talent; Verb meaning to use words, art, or actions to tell others what you are thinking or feeling, or for an idea to be clearly stated.
to be formulated / to formulate oneself / to be stated / to take shape; Verb meaning for an idea, a rule, or a request to be stated in precise words or a clear format.
to be stated / to be enunciated / to be set out / to formulate; Formal verb meaning for a rule, a law, or a principle to be expressed clearly and precisely in words.

to pronounce oneself / to declare / to be pronounced / to speak out; Verb meaning to officially state your opinion or decision about something, or (for a judge or doctor) to give a formal verdict or diagnosis.

to assert oneself / to be confirmed / to be asserted / to show strength; Verb meaning for a person to show their character or power clearly so that others respect them, or for a fact to be stated with absolute certainty.
to be confirmed / to be borne out / to be validated / to come true; Verb meaning for a piece of news, a suspicion, or a trend to be proven true by later events or additional information.
to be verified / to prove true / to be checked / to be authenticated; Verb meaning for a theory or a prediction to be shown to be accurate by the facts of reality.
to become clearer / to take shape / to be specified / to be clarified; Verb meaning for a vague idea, a situation, or a plan to become more detailed and easier to understand.

to explain oneself / to be explained / to be due to / to have an explanation; Verb meaning to give reasons for your behavior, or for a phenomenon to be understood through a specific cause, or for two people to discuss a problem to solve it.

to justify oneself / to be justified / to be warranted / to excuse; Verb meaning to show or prove that an action or a decision is right, fair, or reasonable, especially when others are questioning it.
to be based / to be founded / to rely / to be established; Verb (followed by 'sur') meaning for an argument, a belief, or a law to use something as its starting point or its evidence.

to lean / to be based / to rely / to support oneself; Verb (followed by 'sur') meaning to physically rest your weight on something, or figuratively to use an idea or a person as a source of support or proof.

to rest / to be based (with 'sur') / to rely / to lie (dead); Common verb meaning to stop working or moving to recover energy, or figuratively (followed by 'sur') for a responsibility or a theory to depend entirely on one thing.
to be situated / to be located / to lie / to find oneself; Verb meaning to be in a specific place or to have a specific position in a hierarchy or a period of time.
to be found / to be located / to be / to find oneself; Very common verb meaning to be in a particular place, or to be in a particular state or situation (like feeling tired).

to introduce oneself / to present oneself / to appear / to arise; Verb meaning to tell someone your name, or to go to an office or a court for an interview or a trial, or for an opportunity to happen.
to introduce oneself / to get in / to enter / to insert oneself; Verb meaning to enter a place, sometimes without permission, or to put yourself into a group or a conversation.
